heroTitle: Golden retrievers raised with love in the heart of Beskydy.
heroSubtitle: A small family FCI kennel from the Beskydy Mountains in Moravia, near Rožnov pod Radhoštěm. Puppies grow up at home, among people, with focus on health, balanced temperament and a solid foundation.
whyUsHomeText: Our puppies grow up with us at home, not in a kennel.
whyUsHealthText: Thorough testing, veterinary care, responsible pairing.
whyUsContactText: We stay in touch with all our dog families.
aboutIntro1: The name of our kennel Rosenaw Aurum carries a piece of the place we come from and the love for the breed. "Rosenaw" comes from the historical name of the town Rožnov pod Radhoštěm and "Aurum" means gold in Latin – exactly what Golden Retrievers are to us.
aboutIntro2: The very first was Dexík. A Golden Retriever without a pedigree, but with a huge heart. He taught us how incredibly kind, loyal and sensitive this breed is. Thanks to him, we fell in love.
aboutIntro3: After he passed away, Alma came along. Our dream girl who took us further – not only towards breeding, but also towards a deeper understanding of everything a Golden Retriever can be.
aboutPhilosophy: We are just at the beginning of our breeding journey. We are learning, gaining experience and want to walk this path honestly, with respect for dogs and the breed.
aboutGoal: Our goal is to breed well-balanced, healthy and social dogs that feel equally comfortable in the show ring, in the field and in the middle of a family living room.
aboutClubs: Rosenaw Aurum is a registered kennel of FCI, member of KCHLS and the Retriever Klub CZ.
girlsIntro: Here you will gradually find all our Golden girls – from young hopes to experienced brood bitches and seniors.
almaBasic: born 27 January 2024 • Golden Retriever, female • ČLP/GR/25733
almaPersonality: Alma is our dream Golden Retriever girl. She came into our lives like a whirlwind and quickly became a companion for every occasion – trips, holidays, sports and quiet evenings at home.
almaPersonality2: She has a remarkable gift for sensing the energy of others – whether people or dogs – and naturally adapting to it. This makes her incredibly non-confrontational and harmonious. She loves everyone unconditionally, is friendly and open, yet beautifully calm at home.
almaPersonality3: At the same time, she can’t hide her playful "devil" side when it’s time for action.
almaBreedingInfo: Breeder: Ing. František Vacek, Bohemica Aurum • Owner: Lucie Klesová
puppiesIntro: For us a puppy is a true family member. From the very first days it is in close contact with us, our children and the normal running of our household.
puppiesApproachText1: Our puppies are raised in a family environment. Step by step they are introduced to different sounds, surfaces, people and situations – from quiet evenings on the sofa to exploring the garden and taking short car rides.
puppiesApproachText2: We are happy to support new owners with advice on care, upbringing and training. Our puppies do not leave us empty‑handed – they take a piece of our hearts with them and we like to stay in touch throughout their lives.
puppiesPackList: purchase contract and FCI pedigree; vaccination card / pet passport; starter pack of food and a favourite toy; detailed written information for the first weeks and months
puppiesPlannedText: We are preparing Alma's first litter. Details about the sire will be announced once confirmed.

puppiesArchiveText: For each litter you will find information about parents, dates of birth and links to photo galleries. At the moment we have no litters bred yet.

artHumpolecTitle: Alma shines at the Humpolec retriever show
artBordoviceP1: On Saturday 26 July 2025 we spent the day at the regional club show in Bordovice – Hubertka 2025, where our Alma Bohemica Aurum appeared in the junior class for the last time. And she did brilliantly!
artBordoviceResult:
Alma Bohemica Aurum
(Brandon de Ria Vela × Lollipop Dorado Blanco)
Junior class • V2 • very nice critique
artBordoviceP2: Although the competition was not large this time, Alma received an excellent critique praising her elegant movement, proportions and calm demeanour. She looked composed in the ring and was clearly enjoying herself. She also met her half-sister, which added to the lovely atmosphere of the class.
artBordoviceP3: She was accompanied by her mum Lollipop Dorado Blanco, who competed in the working class and earned a beautiful 3rd place in the Best Working Dog competition. It was also the first time Alma spent a few days with her mum and half-sister at the home kennel – and you could tell she knew exactly where she belonged.
artBordoviceP4: The show had a wonderfully friendly atmosphere. Fans from near and far family came to support us, which we really appreciated. The only thing that did not go to plan was the weather – rain accompanied us all day long. But it certainly did not dampen our spirits.
artBordoviceThanksList: Amálka Vacková for giving our young lady an excellent foundation and for patient breeder support 24/7;Nataliia Romashko for professional grooming – those little paws are perfect
artBordoviceP6: We look forward to more events where she can show what she’s made of!
artProvodoviceP1: This time we headed to the dog show in Provodovice – and it turned out to be a day we will not forget any time soon. Alma entered the open class for the very first time!
artProvodoviceResult:
Alma Bohemica Aurum
(Brandon de Ria Vela × Lollipop Dorado Blanco)
Open class • V1 – Excellent 1 • Class winner • Regional winner
Qualified for final competitions → 3rd place in FCI Group 8
artProvodoviceQuote: “Correct size, nice head, scissor bite, longer firm back, correct chest, correct angulation and nice presentation.”
artProvodoviceP3: Unfortunately the weather was not on our side – it was cold the entire day. Despite that, the event had a wonderful atmosphere and Alma performed absolutely fantastically.
artProvodoviceThanksList: Jana Janíčková from Beskyd Hill for providing a home base;Ondra from Athena Bella for support and encouragement
artProvodoviceP5: We are incredibly proud of Alma. Her open class debut could not have gone any better!
artOvvrP1: On Sunday 1 June 2025, Children’s Day, we set off with Alma for our first big test – OVVR (natural retrieving ability test) in Ústí u Hranic. The weather was lovely with sunshine and great spirits. Ten dogs and their owners gathered, many familiar from training sessions. And as a bonus – two of our trainers also took part!
artOvvrP2: Alma breezed through it – with ease and elegance. The first discipline, temperament assessment, went smoothly. Alma sat calmly at heel and behaved beautifully.
artOvvrP3: The second discipline, behaviour after a gunshot, also went without a hitch. The handler just had to catch the right moment to recall her.
artOvvrP4: The third part – tracking – was where my heart started beating a little faster. Alma excelled here, finding the scent dummy quickly and bringing it back in a straight line. She also performed a field retrieve, which only a few dogs managed.
artOvvrP5: Heeling on and off the lead went perfectly, even though Alma usually likes to explore the terrain with her nose.
artOvvrP6: The final discipline, water retrieve, was the most nerve-wracking. This time she resisted the urge to shake off before handing over the dummy.
artOvvrP7: The entire morning Alma was absolutely amazing. She rested calmly between disciplines. And the result? Absolutely perfect – she passed all disciplines with a full score!
artOvvrP8: We have now met all the breeding requirements except for age. But we are certainly not stopping here. This was just the beginning and we are already looking forward to new challenges, training sessions and adventures.
artHumpolecP1: On Saturday and Sunday (10–11 May 2025) we headed to Humpolec for the Club and Specialty Retriever Show. We entered Alma in the most competitive category – Juniors (because why make it easy?), where around 30 females competed in the ring – basically a casting call for doggy Hollywood.
artHumpolecP2: With a touch of nerves and cautious optimism, we waited to see how it would go. And it went brilliantly! Alma certainly held her own and came away both days with a lovely Excellent rating.
artHumpolecP3: At the show, Alma also finally met her brother Amigo, who went on to win his very first CAC title. Huge congratulations!
artHumpolecP4: We came home with beautiful critiques – both judges particularly praised Alma’s coat and her lively, energetic movement. Her ring presentation was also commended – for which huge thanks go to breeder Amálka, who turned Alma into a real show professional.
artHumpolecP5: We are absolutely thrilled – and the cherry on top is the news that Alma has now met another requirement for breeding approval! She was also measured at the show – she is a tall lady with a beautiful complete set of teeth and a scissor bite, just as a proper retriever should be.
artHumpolecP6: All that is left now is to pass the OVVR working test – and then Alma can start writing her own chapter in breeding history.
artNarozeninyP1: Alma celebrated her very first birthday today. There had to be a cake, of course, and presents too. The kids even organised a little party and invited their friends.
artNarozeninyP2: Dear Alma, we wish you above all good health – and we will happily take care of everything else.
artNarozeninyP3: If you would like to see what it looked like when she was born, take a look at the A-litter diary at the Bohemica Aurum kennel website.
artRtgP1: Today, on International Golden Retriever Day, we took Alma to the vet in Opava (MVDr. Pepřík) to have X-rays taken of her hips and elbows – one of the mandatory requirements for breeding approval. We also had her spine examined, including a check for spondylosis.
artRtgP2: We are overjoyed with the results and will do everything we can to keep Alma in great health for many years to come.
artRtgQuote: And how did she handle it all? Like a true retriever! As soon as she woke up from anaesthesia, she ran straight over to cuddle with a lady in the waiting room.
artRtgP3: The results are available for download in the Documents section.
artGenetickeP1: At the last show in Humpolec, we took the opportunity to have genetic tests done for several hereditary diseases that can occur in Golden Retrievers.
artGenetickeTestList: PRA (prcd, GR-PRA1, GR-PRA2) – progressive retinal atrophy, various forms leading to blindness;Ichthyosis 1 and 2 – hereditary skin conditions causing dry, flaky coat;GRMD – muscular dystrophy, a rare muscle disorder;NCL5 – a nervous system disorder affecting young dogs, extremely rare
artGenetickeResultsList: Eyes (PRA-prcd, GR-PRA1, GR-PRA2): N/N – clear;Ichthyosis 1: N/P – carrier;Ichthyosis 2: N/N – clear;NCL5: N/N – clear;GRMD: Xn/Xn – clear
artGenetickeP3: We are very happy that Alma is a healthy girl. Most of the tested conditions came back completely clear, and for the one where she is a carrier – the result has no impact on her health or well-being whatsoever. For breeding purposes, it simply means the stud dog must be tested as N/N.
artSilherovicePerex: We headed to Šilheřovice with a clear goal: to experience our first Working Test. The result? Two zeros on the exercises. But also one of the most valuable days we have ever had with Alma.
artSilheroviceP1: The event was organised by Retriever klub CZ together with Trénink s retrívrem in the beautiful Šilheřovice forest – with dense undergrowth, ditches, water streams and an open meadow. Terrain made for a Working Test. But also, for Alma, terrain made for being completely distracted from everything we ask of her.
artSilheroviceP2: Judging was handled by an international panel – Maarit Saarinen (Finland), an experienced breeder (Middle River’s), and Paul David Toal (Ireland), FCI judge for field trials and working tests.
artSilheroviceResult:
Alma Bohemica Aurum
(Brandon de Ria Vela × Lollipop Dorado Blanco)
Class E (Elementary) • 4 exercises • 2× 0 points
artSilheroviceP3: In Class E, four exercises awaited us – marking, memory marking and a retrieve – with heelwork assessed throughout. But the very first exercise already got the better of us. After running into two ditches, Alma lost her bearings and could not find the dummy – and her frustration showed in its own way. Let’s just say she had a wee. Well, it happened, and the score equals 0.
artSilheroviceP4: The remaining exercises went better, but the pressure and over-training showed, and her interest in the dummy was not as strong as usual.
artSilheroviceP5: We were there with a great group though – Jana with Zoe and Pinky and Ondra with Bella – so the mood was great despite the zeros.
artSilheroviceP6: And what did we take away from it? A clear training plan:
artSilheroviceTakeaways: more work on steadiness;marking in unfamiliar terrain;heelwork in distracting environments
artSilheroviceP6b: The judges were generous with their time afterwards and the feedback was priceless.
artSilheroviceP7: We will be back. With Alma, there is no other way.
artCanisterapieTitle: Alma passed her canis therapy exam
artCanisterapiePerex: We spent the weekend of 18–19 April with Alma at Sanatoria Klimkovice – a seminar, canis therapy in practice with children, and finally the exam. And Alma has it. Her canis therapy certificate.
artCanisterapieResult:
Alma Bohemica Aurum
(Brandon de Ria Vela × Lollipop Dorado Blanco)
Canis therapy exam certificate • Sanatoria Klimkovice • 19 Apr 2026
artCanisterapieP1: The whole weekend was lovely. The grounds of Sanatoria Klimkovice are beautiful – right next to the complex there is a gorgeous little forest for long walks. Perfect for both the dog and for us to switch off between sessions.
artCanisterapieP2: Saturday was split in two. In the morning we had a seminar with plenty of insights from the practice of canis therapists – concrete situations, what works, what doesn’t and how to handle it all with both the dog and the client.
artCanisterapieP3: The afternoon was even more valuable – children being treated at the sanatorium came to visit us and we got to try canis therapy hands-on. Alma was absolutely brilliant – she lay calmly on her side and let two or even three children rest on her at once. This calm and openness is exactly why we went into canis therapy.
artCanisterapieP4: Sunday brought the exam itself. And I have to admit it was pretty demanding – several less pleasant factors lined up. Part of the exam was testing the dog’s temperament in various tense situations, after which the dog had to settle and let the instructor do positioning work. By that point Alma was a little unsure and not quite willing to cooperate.
artCanisterapieP5: In the end it all worked out – we passed the exam and Alma now holds a canis therapy team certificate. We are looking forward to where canis therapy will take us next.
artCanisterapieP6: I would rather go the educational route with her – into schools. So the first visits will definitely be to my kids’ classrooms. Let’s see where it leads.

docsIntro: Here you will find the complete health documentation of our female Alma Bohemica Aurum. Transparency is a given for us – we want every potential puppy owner to be able to verify everything.
docsPedigree: FCI Certified Pedigree – Alma Bohemica Aurum, ČLP/GR/25733
docsXrayMeta: Examined 3 Feb 2025, MVDr Marek Pepřík, Opava
docsNoteTitle: What our results mean for breeding
docsNoteHdText: HD B means near-normal hip joints with minimal irregularities. It is fully acceptable for breeding. To maximise the chance of the best results in puppies, we will select a stud dog exclusively with HD A (clear) and ideally with proven good results in his line.
docsNoteIctText: Alma is a carrier of ichthyosis 1 – she is completely healthy herself, but carries one copy of the mutated gene. Ichthyosis 1 is a recessive skin condition that only affects dogs with two copies of the mutation (P/P). Therefore, the stud dog must be tested as N/N (clear). In an N/P × N/N mating, 50% of puppies will be clear (N/N) and 50% carriers (N/P) – no puppy can be affected. You can read more about ichthyosis in a seminar paper by the breeder of Bohemica Aurum kennel (in Czech).
docsNoteStrategyText: When selecting a stud dog for Alma, we focus on: HD A (clear), ED 0/0, complete genetic tests with N/N for ICT-1, balanced temperament, quality pedigree and typical conformation. All health results of the stud dog will also be published on this website.

pregTitle: Dog pregnancy calculator — due date & puppy development
pregLead: Free online dog pregnancy calculator. Enter the mating date and instantly find out the expected whelping date, when to schedule an ultrasound and X-ray, and follow your puppies' development week by week — from fertilisation to birth.
pregWeek1Dev: After mating, fertilisation occurs. Sperm travel through the oviduct to the eggs. Fertilised eggs begin to divide.
pregWeek1Tip: Normal routine, quality food. No special changes needed. Avoid vaccinations and chemical treatments.
pregWeek2Dev: Embryos travel through the oviduct towards the uterus. Cells continue to divide, forming germ layers that will become organs.
pregWeek2Tip: No major changes. Ensure a calm environment, avoid stress and excessive physical activity.
pregWeek3Dev: Embryos implant into the uterine wall (around day 16–20). The placenta begins to form, supplying nutrients to the foetuses. The dam may have reduced appetite or morning sickness.
pregWeek3Tip: Offer smaller portions more frequently. If the dam refuses food, don't panic – this is normal. Continue to skip vaccinations.
pregWeek4Dev: Organs, eyes and spine develop. Around day 25, pregnancy can be confirmed by ultrasound and foetal heartbeats detected. Embryos are about 1.5 cm long.
pregWeek4Tip: Ultrasound at the vet (day 25–30) to confirm pregnancy. Limit jumping and rough play.
pregWeek5Dev: Foetuses grow rapidly – paws, claws and whiskers develop. The dam's belly starts to visibly enlarge. Foetuses measure about 3–4 cm.
pregWeek5Tip: Gradually increase protein intake. Start transitioning to higher-quality food (puppy formula). Shorter but more frequent walks.
pregWeek6Dev: Foetuses are fully formed – they have developed fur, pigmentation and reproductive organs. They gain weight rapidly. The dam gains weight noticeably and her belly is clearly larger.
pregWeek6Tip: Feed 3× daily in smaller portions (puppy food). The dam needs more energy, but her stomach has less room. Provide a quiet resting area.
pregWeek7Dev: Foetal skeletons mineralise – visible on X-ray from day 45. This allows an accurate puppy count. Foetuses measure about 7–9 cm with fully developed coats.
pregWeek7Tip: X-ray at the vet (day 45–50) to count puppies. Prepare the whelping box. Limit physical activity to calm walks.
pregWeek8Dev: Puppies are nearly fully developed and move into birthing position. The dam starts 'nesting' – seeking a quiet spot and may become restless. Mammary glands fill with milk.
pregWeek8Tip: The whelping box should be ready and the dam should be accustomed to it. Start taking rectal temperature twice daily. Prepare all whelping supplies.
pregWeek9Dev: Puppies are ready for the world! The dam may refuse food, become restless and seek privacy. A temperature drop below 37 °C signals whelping within 12–24 hours. Golden Retrievers typically have litters of 6–10 puppies.
pregWeek9Tip: Watch for temperature drop (below 37 °C = whelping within 24 hours). Have the vet's number ready. Ensure calm and warmth. If contractions last longer than 2 hours without a puppy being born, call the vet.
pregKeyDeparture: First departure to new homes (from week 8)
pregVideoDesc: Fascinating National Geographic footage showing how puppies develop from fertilisation to birth.
pregVideoBlocked: To play the video you need to accept cookies. Watch on YouTube →
pregChecklistItems: Whelping box (min. 120×120 cm for a Golden Retriever); Clean towels and pads; Digital thermometer; Disinfectant and sterile scissors; Scale for weighing puppies; Coloured collars/ribbons to identify puppies; Vet's and emergency phone numbers; Puppy milk replacer (just in case)
pregGoldenInfo: Gestation length: 58–65 days (average 63 days); Typical litter size: 6–10 puppies; Newborn puppy weight: 350–500 g; Golden Retrievers are generally excellent mothers; C-section is less common in this breed; After whelping the dam needs 3–4× more energy
pregFaqTitle: Frequently asked questions about dog pregnancy
pregFaq1Q: How long is a dog pregnant?
pregFaq1A: A dog’s pregnancy (gestation) lasts an average of 63 days (9 weeks) from the mating date. Whelping may occur between day 58 and day 65. Golden Retrievers average 63 days of gestation.
pregFaq2Q: When to do an ultrasound on a pregnant dog?
pregFaq2A: An ultrasound can be performed between day 25 and 30 after mating. At this stage the vet can confirm pregnancy and detect foetal heartbeats.
pregFaq3Q: When to do an X-ray on a pregnant dog?
pregFaq3A: An X-ray is recommended from day 45 of pregnancy. It allows accurate counting of puppies based on visible skeletal structures.
pregFaq4Q: How many puppies does a Golden Retriever have?
pregFaq4A: A Golden Retriever typically has 6 to 10 puppies per litter. A newborn puppy weighs 350–500 g. Litter size depends on the dam’s age, health, and genetics.
pregFaq5Q: How do I know my dog is about to give birth?
pregFaq5A: The main sign of imminent whelping is a drop in the dam’s body temperature below 37 °C (98.6 °F), signalling birth within 12–24 hours. She may become restless, refuse food, and seek a secluded spot.
pregFaq6Q: When can puppies go to their new homes?
pregFaq6A: Puppies can leave for their new homes at the earliest at 8 weeks of age (56 days after birth). Until then they need to stay with their mother for proper physical and psychological development.
pregDisclaimer: Disclaimer: This guide is for informational purposes only. Every pregnancy is unique. Always consult your veterinarian and follow their recommendations.

breedPageTitle: Golden Retriever – everything about the breed
breedLead: The Golden Retriever is one of the most popular dog breeds in the world. It combines intelligence, a friendly temperament and a natural willingness to work. What makes it so special and what should you know before getting one?
breedHistoryP1: The Golden Retriever originated in 19th-century Scotland thanks to Lord Tweedmouth, who systematically crossed dogs to create the ideal hunting retriever. The breed was officially recognised by The Kennel Club in 1913 and has won hearts all over the world ever since.
breedHistoryP2: The original purpose of the Golden Retriever was retrieving game from water and land. That is why these dogs have a natural love of water, a soft mouth and an exceptional willingness to cooperate with people.
breedTemperP1: The Golden Retriever is known for its friendly, calm and even-tempered nature. It is a dog that loves people – from children to seniors – and gets along wonderfully with other animals. Typical traits include:
breedTemperList: Friendliness – open to everyone, making it an ideal family dog but a poor guard dog;Intelligence – ranked as the 4th most intelligent breed by Stanley Coren;Trainability – responds excellently to positive training and loves learning new things;Patience – tolerates children and their games with admirable patience;Work ethic – needs meaningful activity, otherwise it will find its own (which may not always please the owner);Love of water – most Golden Retrievers love swimming and water retrieves
breedAppearP1: The Golden Retriever is a medium-sized, harmoniously built dog with a characteristic golden coat. The FCI standard (No. 111, Group 8) describes it as "a symmetrical, balanced, active dog with a kindly expression".
breedAppearList: Height at withers: males 56–61 cm, females 51–56 cm;Weight: males 29–34 kg, females 25–29 kg;Coat: flat or wavy with a good water-resistant undercoat;Colour: any shade of gold or cream (not red or mahogany);Lifespan: 10–13 years
breedStandardP1: The full standard defines individual body parts that judges evaluate at shows. Source: Retriever Klub CZ.
breedStandardList: Head and skull: broad skull without coarse features, well-developed deep muzzle, length of foreface roughly equal to skull. Nose black.;Eyes: dark brown, well set apart, with dark rims.;Ears: medium-sized, set approximately level with the eyes.;Jaws: perfect, regular and complete scissor bite – upper incisors closely overlapping the lower.;Neck: good length, clean and muscular.;Body: balanced and well coupled, deep and spacious chest, well-sprung ribs, strong level topline.;Forequarters: straight with good bone, long well-laid-back shoulders.;Hindquarters: strong, muscular loins, well-bent stifles.
breedHealthP1: As with most purebred breeds, the Golden Retriever has hereditary health predispositions that responsible breeders test for. The most important include:
breedHealthList: Hip dysplasia (HD) – X-ray of both parents is a prerequisite for responsible breeding;Elbow dysplasia (ED) – like HD, assessed radiographically;Eye diseases (PRA) – progressive retinal atrophy, tested genetically;Ichthyosis (ICT) – hereditary skin disease, can be ruled out by genetic testing;Cancer – Golden Retrievers unfortunately have a higher predisposition to certain types of tumours
breedHealthP2: That is why choosing a responsible breeder who performs comprehensive health testing is absolutely essential. At our kennel we publish all health results.
breedCareP1: The Golden Retriever is not high-maintenance but does require regular care:
breedCareList: Coat – brushing 2–3 times a week, daily during shedding season. The coat is never clipped, only tidied;Exercise – at least 1–2 hours of active exercise daily (walks, swimming, retrieving);Nutrition – quality food appropriate for age and activity. Golden Retrievers are prone to obesity;Mental stimulation – nose work, obedience, agility or retrieves keep the dog happy;Veterinary care – regular vaccinations, deworming and check-ups
breedSuitTitle: Who is the Golden Retriever suitable for?
breedSuitP1: The Golden Retriever is an ideal choice for:
breedSuitList: Families with children – patient and playful;Active people – can handle hikes, running, swimming and cycling;First-time owners – easy to train, great as a first dog;People looking for a therapy dog – Retrievers excel at working with people
breedSuitP2: On the other hand, it is not suitable for people who spend most of the day away from home, have no time for exercise or are looking for a guard dog.
breedBreederTitle: How to choose a responsible Golden Retriever breeder
breedBreederP1: When choosing a Golden Retriever kennel, look for:
breedBreederList: FCI registration through the national kennel club;Complete health tests of both parents (HD, ED, eye exams, genetic tests);Transparency – the breeder willingly shares results and answers questions;Puppy socialisation – puppies should grow up in a home environment;Lifetime support – a good breeder stays in touch for the dog's entire life;Membership in breed clubs
breedBreederP2: At our kennel Rosenaw Aurum in the Beskydy Mountains we breed Golden Retrievers with a focus on health, temperament and family life. Read about our approach or get in touch.

privacyS1Text:
Lucie Klesová
Vigantice (near Rožnov pod Radhoštěm), Czech Republic
E-mail: lucie@klesova.cz
Phone: +420 724 913 409
privacyS2Text: Through the contact form on this website we may process the following personal data:
privacyS2List: Name — to address you in our reply;E-mail address — to send you a reply;Phone number (optional) — for possible phone contact;Message content — to handle your enquiry
privacyS3Text: We process your personal data solely for the purpose of:
privacyS3List: Replying to your enquiry sent via the contact form;Communication regarding potential interest in a puppy from our kennel;Arranging a visit
privacyS4Text: We process personal data on the basis of legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) — replying to your enquiry. By submitting the contact form you consent to the processing of the provided data for this purpose.
privacyS5Text: We retain your personal data for the time necessary to handle your enquiry, up to 12 months from the last contact. After this period the data are deleted.
privacyS6Text: We do not share your personal data with third parties except:
privacyS6List: Formspree, Inc. — the contact form service provider (processor) that receives and forwards messages from the form. Formspree processes data in accordance with its own privacy policy.
privacyS7Text: This website uses only technically necessary cookies. For font rendering we use Google Fonts, which may process the visitor's IP address. The map in the contact section uses Google Maps.
privacyS8List: Access your personal data;Rectification of inaccurate data;Erasure of data (right to be forgotten);Restriction of processing;Data portability;Object to processing;Lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (www.uoou.cz)
privacyS9Text: To exercise any of the above rights, please contact us at lucie@klesova.cz. We will respond within 30 days at the latest.
toolSpotText: Enter the mating date and instantly get the due date, key dates (ultrasound, x-ray) and puppy development week by week. Works for all dog breeds.
